title: Quobly and CEA-Leti Strengthen Collaboration via FAMES Pilot Line to Scale 300 mm Silicon Spin-Qubit Platform - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Silicon quantum hardware developer Quobly and microelectronics research institute CEA-Leti have expanded their joint technology program, securing Quobly direct access to the European FAMES Pilot Line (FD-SOI Pilot Line for Applications with embedded non-volatile Memories, RF, 3D Integration & PMIC). Hosted at CEA-Leti in Grenoble under the Chips JU initiative, the pilot line complements Quobly’s commercial manufacturing partnership with STMicroelectronics, providing advanced processing tools to prototype 3D integration, radio-frequency (RF) control layers, and process flows for next-generation quantum processing units (QPUs).

Quobly’s architecture, QSOI®, integrates silicon spin qubits directly onto a 300 mm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) CMOS substrate. The platform combines spin-qubit arrays with cryogenic control electronics on a unified die, leveraging Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) manufacturing principles. By leveraging the FAMES infrastructure’s 3D integration and embedded non-volatile memory capabilities, Quobly aims to scale qubit density and pulse-control performance on standard 300 mm foundry lines without expanding thermal or physical footprints.

Access to FAMES establishes an intermediate prototyping bridge between exploratory R&D and commercial foundry runs at STMicroelectronics. Quobly plans to offer initial cloud availability for its first-generation processor family, Alloy Pioneer, by late 2026, targeting a long-term scaling trajectory toward large-scale, fault-tolerant silicon architectures by 2032.
